Improving veteran health through nutrition is critical, but real progress requires dismantling the bureaucratic bloat that’s plagued VA healthcare for decades. The Veterans Access to Direct Primary Care Act (H.R. 961) offers a smarter path by letting veterans bypass the VA’s broken system and access private primary care through health savings accounts.

While Buchanan’s op-ed touts “Food as Medicine,” the real issue is systemic waste: Medicare and Medicaid are projected to burn $4.1 trillion on obesity-related diseases by 2033. Instead of expanding government-run programs, we need market-driven reforms that empower veterans to choose efficient, personalized care—not more D.C. middlemen.

Nutrition matters, but so does cutting the red tape that strangles innovation.

Focusing on nutrition is key, but let’s not pretend D.C. isn’t part of the problem. The same politicians pushing “Food is Medicine” programs also let Big Pharma and processed food giants rig the system. Medicare fraud, overpriced hospital contracts, and junk food subsidies cost taxpayers billions while real solutions get buried.

If we’re serious about health, cut the middlemen and expose the corruption—starting with bloated federal nutrition programs that line bureaucrats’ pockets instead of feeding families.

Real reform means breaking monopolies, not expanding government slush funds.
